s4-see-1: Dad, can I have a burger after the match today?
Hmm, a burger isn't great after sport. What about a chicken salad?
A salad? OK, maybe. Oh, wait. Coach says pasta gives you energy. I'll have pasta instead.
Pasta it is, then. Good choice.
s4-see-2: Mum, the science museum opens at nine o'clock on Sunday, doesn't it? Can we leave at half past eight?
No, actually it only opens at nine on weekdays. On Sundays it opens at ten.
Oh! Then let's leave at half past nine.
Good idea. We'll be there just in time.
s4-see-3: Hello, everyone, and welcome to the Nature Club. We meet every Wednesday at quarter past three in Room 12. This term your leader is Mr Pellow. That's P-E-double L-O-W. He knows a lot about birds and insects. Please bring a notebook and a pencil every week. You needn't bring binoculars, because the club has ten pairs.
s4-ch-1a: Mum, I'm going to take biscuits to the class picnic tomorrow.
Hmm, everyone always brings biscuits. What about some bananas?
Bananas get squashed in my bag. Oh, I know! I'll take apples instead. They're healthy and they don't get squashed.
Good idea. There's a big bag of apples in the kitchen.
s4-ch-1b: Grandpa, we're getting a pet next week! I really wanted a rabbit.
A rabbit? Lovely. Will it live in the garden?
Well, we haven't got a garden, so Mum said no. Then I thought about a hamster, but they sleep all day. So in the end we chose two goldfish.
Fish are easy to look after.
s4-ch-2a: Miss Lane, is the school concert on Tuesday?
No, Omar. Tuesday is our last practice. The concert is on Thursday evening, in the main hall.
Thursday? Oh, my grandma's arriving on Friday. I hope she can come a day early!
I hope so too. Tell her the tickets are free.
s4-ch-2b: Dad, guess how much my new goggles were. Sixteen pounds!
Sixteen pounds? That's a lot of money for goggles!
Oh no, sorry, I mean six pounds. The blue ones were nine pounds, but I got the green ones. They were cheaper.
Six pounds is a good price.
s4-ch-3a: Hello, everyone, and welcome to the tennis club. I'm your coach this year, and you can call me Coach Tolley. That's T-O-double L-E-Y. Please write my name on your club card, because you'll need it if you want to book a court. We meet every Monday after school.
s4-ch-3b: Good afternoon, and welcome to the computer club. My name is Ms Rendall. Let me spell that for you: R-E-N-D-A-double L. This term we're going to make short animated films about animals. If you have a question, you can send me a message on the school website.
s4-ch-4a: Mum, can you drive me to school tomorrow? It's going to rain.
Sorry, Tariq, the car's at the garage until Friday.
Oh. Then I'll get the bus, like I usually do.
Actually, there's no school bus tomorrow. The drivers have a meeting. Your sister will walk with you. Don't forget your umbrella!
s4-ch-4b: Lan, you're full of energy today! What did you have for breakfast?
Well, I usually have noodle soup, but this morning my grandma cooked eggs for me.
Lucky you! I only had a piece of toast.
Eggs are great before sports day. Grandma says they help your muscles.
s4-r1-1a: Mai, what time does the chess club start on Wednesdays?
At quarter to four, in the library. We finish at five o'clock.
And the late bus home leaves at quarter past five?
Yes, so don't play one more game at the end! The bus won't wait.
s4-r1-1b: Dad, what time are we going to the cinema? I can't wait to see the film about whales.
We'll leave home at six o'clock. The film starts at half past six.
And what time does it finish?
At half past seven, just in time for dinner.
s4-r1-2a: Excuse me, how much are the tickets for the zoo, please?
Adults are twelve pounds, and children are eight pounds.
Thank you. And how much is the map of the zoo?
It's four pounds. But there's a big map on the wall by the gate, and that's free.
s4-r1-2b: Dad, look at this blue water bottle! It's fifteen pounds.
That's too much, Noah. Look, the red one is only five pounds, and it's the same size.
OK, I'll get the red one. It's got a free sticker too.
Good. Here's a ten-pound note, so you'll get some change.
s4-r1-3a: Duc, when is our class trip to the farm?
It's on Wednesday. Remember, we've got art on Monday, so bring your apron then.
Great. Will we see the baby goats?
I hope so. And Mr Ross says he'll put the photos from the farm on the class website on Friday.
s4-r1-3b: Thu, can you collect the eggs from the hens, please?
OK, Grandma. Look! I found twelve eggs!
Twelve? Wonderful! Yesterday there were only two. The hens must like this warm weather.
We've got twenty hens, haven't we? Maybe tomorrow there'll be twenty eggs!
Maybe! Now, let's make an omelette.
s4-r2-1a: Mum, I'm going to join the drama club this term.
Yes. Oh, but that's when I have football practice. So I've changed my mind. I'll join the science club on Thursdays instead. We're going to build a model bridge!
s4-r2-1b: Dad, I want to get Chloe a teddy for her birthday.
She's got lots of teddies, Jack. What about a puzzle?
Hmm, she finished her last puzzle in one day! Oh, I know. She loves flowers. I'll buy her a little plant in a pot.
Perfect. She can look after it herself.
s4-r2-2a: Coach, where are the badminton rackets? Are they in the cupboard?
Not today, Minh. I put them on the stage this morning.
I've looked on the stage. There are only the nets there.
Oh, sorry, you're right! Actually, they're in the big bag by the door.
s4-r2-2b: Mum, the bike race starts at ten o'clock, so we can leave at half past nine.
Let me check the poster. No, Kenji, the race starts at quarter past ten. Ten o'clock is when you collect your number.
OK, but let's still leave at half past nine. I don't want to be late!
s4-r2-3a: Dad, look at my photo from the river trip!
No, we didn't see any otters. There were lots of ducks, but they swam away before I could take a photo. This is a kingfisher. It's that bright blue bird, see?
s4-r2-3b: Ethan, did your dad drive you to the sports centre today?
No, he was busy. I was going to take the bus, but it was really late. So I rode my bike. It only took ten minutes!
Clever. I walked here with my mum. It took us half an hour!
s4-r3-1a: Mum, our new art club teacher is really nice.
That's good. What's her name? I'd like to say hello at the school gate.
No, F-A-I-R, like the word fair. F-A-I-R-L-E-Y. She's going to teach us how to paint animals and birds.
s4-r3-1b: Dad, what's the name of the new vet? I want to write it on the fridge.
He's called Mr Dobson. That's D-O-B-S-O-N. He works at the animal clinic on Park Road.
No, only one B, and there's no second S. D-O-B-S-O-N. He was very kind to our cat.
s4-r3-2a: Hello, Grade 5. I have some news about the chess club. From next week, there's a new coach. His name is Mr Oakes. That's O-A-K-E-S. Also, the club is moving from Monday to Thursday, because the hall is busy on Mondays. Please tell your parents.
s4-r3-2b: Good morning. On Saturday we're going on a bird-watching walk in Elm Park. Your leader is Ms Penrose. That's P-E-N-R-O-S-E. We'll meet at the park gate at quarter past eight, not half past, because birds are busiest early in the morning. Please wear warm clothes and bring something to drink.
s4-r3-3a: Right, everyone. For sports day on Friday, please wear your school PE kit, not your own clothes. Bring a water bottle and a hat, because it's going to be sunny. You don't need to bring snacks. We'll give everyone some fruit at lunchtime. See you all on the field on Friday morning.
s4-r3-3b: Next Tuesday we're visiting the Museum of Old Machines. The trip costs eight pounds. It was going to be ten pounds, but the school is paying some of it. Please bring a notebook, because you'll draw one machine that you like. You can have lunch at the museum café.
s4-a1-1a: Mum, I'm back from the market!
Thanks, Maya. Did you get the strawberries?
Sorry, they were all sold out. I nearly bought some grapes, but they looked a bit old. So I got a big watermelon instead.
A watermelon! Perfect for this hot weather. Let's put it in the fridge.
s4-a1-1b: Dad, have you seen my football boots? I think I left them in the garden.
I was in the garden this morning. Only your ball was there.
Then maybe they're under my bed?
Hmm, no. Oh, wait, I remember! You took them off in the car after the match. They're still on the back seat.
s4-a1-2a: Mum, my piano lesson is at four o'clock as usual on Thursday, isn't it?
Not this week. Your teacher phoned. She's going to the dentist, so the lesson starts at half past four.
Oh. Will it still finish at five?
No, it'll finish at half past five this week.
s4-a1-2b: Look, Grandpa, I bought the book about sharks!
Wonderful. Was it expensive? It was twelve pounds on the website.
In the shop it was nine pounds. But today everything was half price, so I only paid four pounds fifty!
What a good price. Now you can read it to me after dinner!
s4-a1-3a: Hi, Hana! Did you go to the cycling race on Saturday?
No, it was too windy, so they cancelled it.
Oh no! What did you do then?
My brother wanted to play tennis, but I went climbing at the sports centre with my cousin. I got to the top of the wall! It was amazing.
s4-a1-3b: Miss Ford, I've finished my poster about animals that live in cold places.
Great! Did you draw the polar bear in the end?
I tried, but it looked like a dog! So I drew a penguin instead. I wrote about seals too, but there's no picture of them.
s4-a2-1a: Dev, is the science club in Room 14 today, like last week?
No, Room 14 is being painted. Mr Shaw said Room 40.
Room 40? But that's the music room.
Oh, sorry. He said Room 4, not 40. It's the one next to the library.
s4-a2-1b: Mum, can I go to the park with Bao after school today?
Not today, Lucas. You've got your appointment at the dentist, remember?
But I thought that was tomorrow.
No, it's today at four. You can go to the park tomorrow. And don't forget your guitar lesson on Thursday.
s4-a2-2a: How was your holiday in Da Nang, Anh? Did you fly there?
That was the plan, but all the planes were full.
So did your dad drive you there?
No, it's too far by car. We went by train instead. It took all night, but I slept in a little bed on the train!
s4-a2-2b: Rosa, the ice rink opens at nine o'clock. Let's go early tomorrow.
Dad, tomorrow's Sunday. On Sundays it opens an hour later.
Ah, ten o'clock, then. Good, that gives us time for a big breakfast.
Yes. And it's really busy from eleven, so we should get there when it opens.
s4-a2-3a: Mum, I can't hear anything on my tablet. Do I need a new one?
Of course not! Have you checked the cable for your headphones?
Yes, the cable's fine. I tried it with Dad's headphones and they worked. I think my headphones are broken.
Then we'll buy you new headphones, not a new tablet.
s4-a2-3b: Ruby, you're twenty minutes late. Did you miss the bus?
No, Mr Shaw. I don't take the bus on Wednesdays, I walk. And I woke up early.
It rained so much last night that the path by the river was closed. I had to walk the long way round.
s4-a3-pondday: Good morning, everyone. I've got some news about our Pond Life Day at Greenbank Nature Park. We were going to go on Tuesday, but another school is visiting the park that day, so we're going on Thursday instead. Please tell your parents about the new day. When we arrive, a guide will meet us at the gate. Her name is Mrs Pritchard. That's P-R-I-T-C-H-A-R-D. She has worked at the park for twenty years, and she knows everything about frogs, newts and dragonflies. Last year she found a very rare frog at the park, and she'll tell us all about it. In the morning, we'll walk round the big pond and look for animals. After lunch, we'll use nets to catch tiny water animals, and we'll look at them through a magnifying glass. Don't worry, we'll put them all back in the water afterwards. Now, what do you need? You'll probably get wet, so please wear old clothes. You needn't bring a net or a magnifying glass, because the park will give us those. But you must bring a towel to dry your hands, and a packed lunch, of course. We'll leave school by bus at nine o'clock and we'll be back by three. If you have any questions, come and see me at lunchtime. I'm sure it will be a brilliant day.
s4-a3-funrun: Hello, runners! Thank you for signing up for the Junior Fun Run at Riverside Park next Saturday. Here's what you need to know. The race starts at ten o'clock, but please meet at the park café at half past nine, so we have time to warm up together. Don't be late, because we can't give out race numbers after quarter to ten. I'm afraid I won't be there on the day, because I'm running in a race in another city. My friend Mr Faulkner will be in charge instead. That's F-A-U-L-K-N-E-R. He's a great runner and a very kind coach. If you have a problem, look for him next to the café. The run is three kilometres, and it goes twice around the lake. Walking is fine, so don't worry if you get tired. Everybody who finishes gets a medal, and your parents are welcome to come and cheer. What should you wear? Comfortable trainers, of course, and shorts or a tracksuit. Everyone must also wear a T-shirt from the club, so the helpers can see you easily. Last year the T-shirts were green, but this year they're yellow. You can collect yours from me on Friday. Oh, and bring a bottle of water, and please write your name on it. See you there!
s4-t-1a: Rory, do you play badminton on Wednesdays?
No, I play badminton on Mondays. On Wednesdays I've got basketball at the sports centre.
Cool! I do table tennis on Wednesdays. It's in the same building.
Great. Let's go there together next week, then. My mum can take us both in the car.
s4-t-1b: Vy, are you still learning the piano?
No, I stopped last year. Now I'm learning the violin. I practise every evening.
My brother plays the drums. It's so noisy in our house when he practises!
Well, the violin isn't very quiet either when you're a beginner!
s4-t-2a: Miss Grey, what time does the bus to the zoo leave tomorrow?
It leaves at quarter to nine. So please be at school by quarter past eight.
And what time do we get to the zoo?
At about quarter past nine, if the roads are quiet.
s4-t-2b: Mum, I've bought the tickets for the dinosaur museum.
Great. Three tickets, for you, me and Dad?
No, I bought four. Grandma wants to come too! She loves dinosaurs.
Lovely. And your cousin is meeting us for lunch, so I'll book a table for five at the café.
s4-t-3a: Dad, I bought a kite at the beach shop. It cost seven pounds.
Seven? The big one in the window was ten pounds.
That one was too heavy. And for that one the string was three pounds extra, but my kite came with string!
Clever girl. Let's fly it now.
s4-t-3b: Can I have a banana smoothie, please? How much is it?
A small one is two pounds, and a large one is three pounds. A bottle of water is just one pound.
I'm really thirsty after football. A large smoothie, please.
Here you are. Enjoy your smoothie!
s4-t-4a: Mum, I'm going to the library after school. I need some books about frogs for my project.
The library's closed on Tuesdays, Leah.
Then can I go to the pond in the park and look at real frogs?
Not today, it's going to rain. Use the computer at home.
OK, I'll do my project at home.
s4-t-4b: Oh no, Mum! I left something at the sports centre.
No, I'm wearing my jacket, look. And my gloves are in my pocket. It's my cap, the blue one with the white stripe.
Don't worry, Max. We'll get it tomorrow on the way to school.
s4-t-5a: Dad, what are we doing on Sunday? Are we going to the beach?
It's going to be cold and windy, so not the beach.
Can we go to the cinema, then?
We went last week. Let's go to the new science museum. It's got a room full of old phones and computers.
s4-t-5b: Grandma, I made something in my cooking class today. Guess!
Was it a pizza? You love pizza.
We made pizza last week. Today the teacher wanted to make a cake, but the oven was broken. So we made a fruit salad.
That's very healthy! You can make one for me at the weekend.
s4-t-flight: Hello, Grade 5. I'd like to tell you about our trip to the Museum of Flight. We'll find out how planes and hot-air balloons were invented, and how they changed the way people travel. The trip was on the calendar for Monday the twelfth, but the museum is closed on Mondays, so we've moved it to the next day, Tuesday. Please be at school by eight o'clock. The bus leaves at quarter past eight, because the museum is two hours away. We'll be back at about four o'clock. The trip was going to cost eighteen pounds, but the museum has given us a special price, so it's fifteen pounds. That includes your ticket and a ride in the flight simulator, which is like sitting in a real plane. At the museum, a guide will show us round. His name is Mr Wakefield. That's W-A-K-E-F-I-E-L-D. He used to be a pilot, so he can answer all your questions about flying. We'll have lunch in the museum garden, so bring a packed lunch. Please also bring a pencil, because there's a quiz to do as we walk round. You needn't bring a camera, because you mustn't take photos inside the museum. If you have any questions, come and find me tomorrow. I'm sure you'll enjoy it.
s4-t-aquarium: Good afternoon, everyone. Here's some important information about our trip to the City Aquarium. First, the day. Lots of you think the trip is on Friday, because that's what the first letter said. But the aquarium has a special talk about sharks on Wednesday, so we're going then instead. We'll meet in the school hall at half past seven, and the bus leaves at quarter to eight. Please be on time, because the bus can't wait. Now, the money. A ticket costs twelve pounds. The shark talk is two pounds more, so that's fourteen pounds altogether. Everyone in our class wants to see the shark talk, so please bring fourteen pounds. At the aquarium we'll meet the shark expert. Her name is Ms Merrick. That's M-E-double R-I-C-K. She has swum with sharks in three different oceans! We'll also see a huge tank with more than five hundred fish, and you can even touch a starfish. What should you bring? It's quite cold inside the aquarium, because the water is kept cool for the fish, so please bring a jumper. You don't need to bring lunch, because the aquarium café will give us sandwiches. And please leave your phones at home. If you have any questions, ask me at the end of the day. See you on the trip!
